plan.title: Welcome empty state in sidebar when festinalente not initialized
plan.overview: Add a welcome/empty state to the VSCode sidebar when .festinalente/ does not exist. The Tasks view shows a welcome message with guidance to run "npx festinalente init". All other views (Quicks, Config, Directives, Product Docs, Engineering Docs) are hidden via "when" clauses on the festinalente.hasFestinalenteFolder context key. A file system watcher on the workspace root detects .festinalente/ creation and dynamically initializes all orchestrators without requiring a window reload.

approach.rationale:
Two changes work together:
1. **package.json declarative config**: Add "when": "festinalente.hasFestinalenteFolder" to all non-Tasks views so they hide when not initialized. Update the existing viewsWelcome text for Tasks to show the "npx festinalente init" guidance. The existing setContext call at extension.ts:56 already sets this context to false when no folder is found.
2. **extension.ts restructure**: Extract the orchestrator setup (lines 60-213) into a reusable function. The activate() function always sets up a workspace-root file watcher for .festinalente/ creation. When the watcher fires, it calls the setup function, updates the context key, and disposes itself. This follows the existing file watcher pattern at tasks.orchestrator.ts:348-356 using RelativePattern.
This approach keeps extension.ts as a thin composition root (directive A5) while enabling dynamic re-initialization. No new modules are needed since this is purely a restructuring of the existing activate() function.

task.name: Add "when" clauses to hide non-Tasks views and update welcome text
task.action:
- Add "when": "festinalente.hasFestinalenteFolder" to 5 view definitions in contributes.views.festinalente: - festinalenteQuicks - festinalenteConfig - festinalenteDirectives - festinalenteProductDocs - festinalenteEngineeringDocs - Do NOT add a "when" clause to festinalenteTasks (it must always be visible) - Update the existing viewsWelcome entry for festinalenteTasks (line 91-96) to show: "Get started by initializing Festina Lente:

npx festinalente init"
Current viewsWelcome (approximate): ```json { "view": "festinalenteTasks", "contents": "No .festinalente folder found in this workspace.

Open a folder containing a .festinalente directory to see tasks.", "when": "!festinalente.hasFestinalenteFolder" } ```
Change to: ```json { "view": "festinalenteTasks", "contents": "Get started by initializing Festina Lente:

npx festinalente init", "when": "!festinalente.hasFestinalenteFolder" } ```
Current views (approximate): ```json { "id": "festinalenteQuicks", "name": "Quicks" } ```
Change to: ```json { "id": "festinalenteQuicks", "name": "Quicks", "when": "festinalente.hasFestinalenteFolder" } ```
Apply the same "when" pattern to Config, Directives, Product Docs, and Engineering Docs views.
task.done: Tasks view shows welcome text when not initialized; other 5 views are hidden when not initialized; all views visible when initialized

edge-cases.case: No watcher set up, Tasks view shows welcome text via viewsWelcome (findFestinalenteFolder returns undefined)
findFestinalenteFolder already iterates all folders; watcher uses first folder only which is acceptable since most users have single-root workspaces
Watcher fires, findFestinalenteFolder re-checks existence before initializing, so false trigger is handled

pitfall.issue: Double initialization if watcher fires multiple times

pitfalls.pitfall: Guard with a boolean flag or dispose watcher immediately on first successful init (FR6 requires disposal)
Use '.festinalente/**' pattern since createFileSystemWatcher may not fire for directory creation alone; watching for any file creation inside .festinalente/ is more reliable
initializeOrchestrators is an extracted function, not a new module. Extension.ts remains the composition root with no policy logic added.
